title: Behind the Curtain — The Pyramid of Power
subtitle: From public authority to the unresolved symbolic apex
editorialBoundary: This model maps documented authority, ownership, voting rights, appointments, capital, infrastructure, intelligence access, policy influence and institutional continuity. It does not infer criminality, secret coordination, ritual involvement or supernatural command from wealth, family name, religion, nationality, social contact or symbolism.

updatePolicy.refreshRule: When reviewed evidence changes a role, score, ownership path, family-control structure or relationship, rebuild the model, preserve the previous snapshot and publish the new dated state.

viewModes.label: Show Only What Can Be Proven

levels.name: The Lightbringer
levels.question: Is the final ruler a person, an entity, an ideology or the system itself?
levels.thesis: The apex is presented as an open symbolic hypothesis: knowledge, illumination, technological transcendence, false light, elite self-perception or the impersonal logic of the machine.
levels.counterweight: No empirical record establishes a supernatural being as the command authority over the named people and institutions below.

levels.name: The Human Apex
levels.question: Which living people can reach the greatest number of consequential systems?
levels.thesis: This tier is generated from current verified roles and access mechanisms. It is a ranking of reach, not a declaration of secret rulership.
levels.counterweight: Each candidate remains constrained by law, institutions, bureaucracy, markets, alliances, succession and rival power centres.

levels.name: The Inner Councils Question
levels.kicker: Verified bodies and alleged coordinating centres
levels.question: Where do high-level decisions become collective, private or technically insulated?
levels.thesis: The page names actual councils, committees and boards, then separates their documented mandates from claims that they form one supreme command structure.
levels.counterweight: No single supreme human council has been verified; these bodies possess different mandates, memberships and vetoes.

levels.name: The Thirteen Families Claim
levels.question: Is thirteen a verified command structure, a symbolic number or a later synthesis?
levels.thesis: Thirteen named dynastic structures and historical houses are compared because they recur in discussions of continuity. Inclusion does not establish a council of thirteen.
levels.counterweight: The current record does not establish a unified council of exactly thirteen families controlling all major systems.

levels.name: Dynastic and Hereditary Networks
levels.question: Which families retain enforceable authority or voting control across generations?
levels.thesis: The strongest family power appears where succession, voting rights, trusts, foundations or holding companies legally preserve control.
levels.counterweight: Family-level control is usually sectoral or jurisdictional, not proof of command over unrelated states and institutions.

levels.name: The Connectors
levels.question: Who links capital, policy, boards, states and technical infrastructure?
levels.thesis: Connector power comes from repeated cross-system access rather than public office alone.
levels.counterweight: Connection is not command; every pathway must identify the actual right, role, transaction or decision.

levels.name: The Policy Architects
levels.question: Who designs the frameworks that later become policy, regulation or institutional practice?
levels.thesis: Policy power is measured through mandates, papers, committees, regulation and implementation, not conference attendance.
levels.counterweight: Proposals may be rejected, altered or constrained by legislatures, courts, member states and markets.

levels.name: Intelligence, Security and Covert Capability
levels.kicker: Information and force outside ordinary visibility
levels.question: Who can see what the public cannot see and authorize capabilities unavailable to ordinary actors?
levels.thesis: This layer maps lawful command, classified access, military authority, intelligence-sharing and security continuity.
levels.counterweight: Former service, social contact or media claims do not prove current covert command.

levels.name: Ownership and Critical Infrastructure
levels.kicker: The rails society cannot easily replace
levels.question: Who controls compute, chips, payments, energy, logistics and other indispensable systems?
levels.thesis: Ownership, voting rights and operational authority are traced beyond the brand name to the responsible board, shareholder, state or executive.
levels.counterweight: Critical firms are interdependent and constrained by regulators, customers, suppliers, states and technical limits.

levels.name: Money and Capital Gatekeepers
levels.question: Who can fund, starve, refinance, sanction or redirect major pools of capital?
levels.thesis: This layer distinguishes personal ownership from delegated fiduciary authority and public monetary power.
levels.counterweight: Assets under management are not personal property, and monetary institutions operate through law and committees.

levels.name: The Permanent Administrative System
levels.question: Which institutions, legal mandates and professional systems survive changes of government?
levels.thesis: Durable institutions preserve archives, procedures, appointments, standards, security relationships and operational capacity.
levels.counterweight: Institutional continuity does not mean institutions are immune from law, politics, failure, reform or public pressure.

levels.name: The Public Stage
levels.question: Who appears to govern?
levels.thesis: Public leaders possess real authority, but the page tests which powers are temporary, shared, delegated or dependent on structures below the headlines.
levels.counterweight: Visibility is not the same as ownership, continuity or unrestricted control.

chokePoints.name: Policy Design and Standards

chokePoints.question: What survives the fall of a leader or the death of a founder?

symbolicDossiers.name: The Lightbringer
symbolicDossiers.summary: A contested archetype of illumination, forbidden knowledge, rebellion, technology, elite self-conception and false light.
symbolicDossiers.notEstablished: No empirical evidence establishes the Lightbringer as the operational commander of the named human network.

symbolicDossiers.name: Lucifer / Morning Star
symbolicDossiers.summary: A term with changing textual, theological and esoteric meanings.
symbolicDossiers.notEstablished: Use of light or star imagery does not prove worship, membership or criminal conduct.

symbolicDossiers.name: Saturn / Kronos
symbolicDossiers.summary: Associated in different traditions with time, limits, law, hierarchy and the devouring father.
symbolicDossiers.notEstablished: Symbolic resemblance does not demonstrate a literal Saturnian command structure.

symbolicDossiers.name: Baal
symbolicDossiers.summary: An ancient title later reinterpreted through polemic, theology and modern conspiracy literature.
symbolicDossiers.notEstablished: The term cannot prove that modern institutions share one ancient cult.

symbolicDossiers.name: Moloch
symbolicDossiers.summary: A disputed historical subject often used as a metaphor for systems that consume human lives or future generations.
symbolicDossiers.notEstablished: A metaphor of sacrifice does not prove literal ritual activity by named people.

symbolicDossiers.name: The Black Cube
symbolicDossiers.summary: A geometric motif linked by modern interpreters to Saturn, containment, law and institutional enclosure.
symbolicDossiers.notEstablished: Similar geometry across cultures does not prove common authorship or command.

symbolicDossiers.name: The Pyramid
symbolicDossiers.summary: A model of hierarchy, concentration and ascent used here to organize evidence.
symbolicDossiers.notEstablished: The shape itself is not evidence of conspiracy.

symbolicDossiers.name: The Architect
symbolicDossiers.summary: The figure who designs systems, rules, thresholds and durable structures while remaining less visible than public operators.
symbolicDossiers.notEstablished: Architectural language alone does not identify a secret individual.

thirteenFamiliesReview.headline: Thirteen named structures under investigation — not a verified council
thirteenFamiliesReview.method: Compare enforceable office, voting rights, ownership, succession, board influence, decline and counter-evidence. Do not merge contradictory lists into false consensus.
thirteenFamiliesReview.currentFinding: The model documents several powerful dynastic structures and historically important houses. It does not verify a unified group of exactly thirteen controlling the world.
